question: How much annual leave can I carry over into the next leave year?
answer: You can carry over a maximum of 240 annual leave hours from one leave year to the next [2].

question: I've been a federal employee for 5 years. How much annual leave do I earn each pay period?
answer: You earn 6 hours of annual leave each pay period. [1]

question: What is the most award leave I can receive in one fiscal year?
answer: You can receive up to 80 hours of award leave in a single fiscal year[1].

question: If I leave TTS, will my unused award leave be paid out?
answer: No, unused award leave is not paid out if you leave TTS[1].

question: How much sick leave can I use per year for a family member's funeral?
answer: You can use up to 13 days (104 hours) of sick leave per year for bereavement, including attending a family member’s funeral[1].

question: How much parental bereavement leave do I get if my child passes away?
answer: You are entitled to two weeks (80 hours) of parental bereavement leave when your child passes away[1].

question: How many days of military leave do I get each year as a National Guard member or Reservist?
answer: You receive 15 days of Military Leave each year for active duty, active‑duty training, and inactive‑duty training as a National Guard member or Reservist[1].

question: What disability rating do I need for disabled veteran leave, and how many hours can I get?
answer: You need a service‑connected disability rating of at least 30 percent, and you can receive up to 104 hours of disabled veteran leave [1].

question: If I'm approved for administrative leave to vote on election day, what is the maximum amount of time I can take?
answer: If administrative leave is granted for voting, it may be used for only the time needed to vote and cannot exceed three work hours[2].

question: What is the maximum number of credit hours I can have accrued at one time?
answer: You can have up to 24 credit hours accrued at any given time[1].

question: When does regular comp time expire, and what happens to it if I leave GSA?
answer: Comp time expires one year (26 pay periods) after it is earned, and if you leave GSA your comp time will be paid out [2].

question: What happens to my unused travel comp time if I leave GSA?
answer: If you leave GSA, any unused travel comp time is forfeited [1].

question: What is the most advanced sick leave I can request?
answer: You can request up to 240 hours of advanced sick leave, although if you are a term employee you may only request up to the total amount you will earn during the remainder of your term [1][2].

question: How long do I need to have worked for the federal government to be eligible for FMLA?
answer: You must have at least one year of federal service to be eligible for FMLA[1][2].

question: If I take all 12 weeks of paid parental leave, how much FMLA do I have left for the next 52 weeks?
answer: If you use the full 12 weeks of Paid Parental Leave, it consumes the entire 12‑week FMLA entitlement, leaving you with no FMLA remaining for the next 52 weeks [2][5].

question: After paid parental leave, how long do I have to agree to return to work?
answer: You must sign an agreement to return to work for at least 12 weeks after your final day of paid parental leave[4].

question: How much bereavement leave can I use per year for a civilian family member, and how much funeral leave do I get for an immediate relative's combat-related death?
answer: You can use up to 13 days (104 hours) of sick leave per year for bereavement for a civilian family member [2]. For an immediate relative who suffered a combat‑related death, you are entitled to 3 days (24 hours) of funeral leave [1].

question: Above what dollar amount do I need a receipt for a travel expense?
answer: Receipts are required for any travel expense that exceeds $75 [1].

question: What percentage of the normal M&IE rate do I get on travel days?
answer: You receive 75 % of the normal M&IE rate on travel days[1].

question: How soon after returning from a trip should I submit my travel voucher?
answer: You should submit your travel voucher within 5 business days after you get back from your trip[2].

question: Can supervisors get reimbursed for professional liability insurance, and how much?
answer: Supervisors may be reimbursed for professional liability insurance for up to half the cost, with a maximum reimbursement of $150 [1].

question: How far in advance do I need to contact the Travel and Events team for official international travel?
answer: You should reach out to the Travel and Events team at least 7 weeks before your official international travel [1].

question: What counts as a 'large team gathering' that needs the event request process instead of an approval email?
answer: A “large team gathering” is any event where more than six employees travel for an internal management meeting (not day‑to‑day business) and/or the estimated travel expenses for the group exceed $10,000[1].
